source_en: End of rotation. Standard transit through the civilian checkpoint.
Scheduled personnel transfer. You should have the clearance on file.
Shift handover. My relief is already at the post.
Extended patrol perimeter. I cross here twice a day now.
Security reassignment following the eastern incident. Transit is routine.
We've been running double rotations. This is the third crossing today.
Lockdown rotation. I go where command sends me.
Sector reassignment under the emergency order. Papers are current.
Standard transit. You'll be seeing a lot of us from now on.
Resigned from the service. Looking for factory work.
Delivering bread for the bakery co-op. Morning round.
First time at a checkpoint. Please explain the procedure.
Resting this week. Command cancelled all patrols east.
Collecting my maternity leave papers.
Off duty for good. I take orders from no one now.
Ignoring the emergency order. I go where I please.
Volunteering at the church. The state means nothing to me.
Visiting family in the city. My unit can wait.
Let's make this quick. I have a post to get back to.
You going to stare, or are you going to check the papers?
Standard transit. You've done this before, I assume.
Twice today already. You'd think they'd streamline this.
Still running the same process, I see. Fine.
Don't ask unnecessary questions. We'll both be happier.
Just do what you're supposed to do.
I've been through a lot of checkpoints today. This one better be fast.
Papers. Stamp. Done. That's all this needs to be.
Good. See, that wasn't so hard.
Faster than yesterday. You're learning.
Adequate. Keep it up.
You're detaining state personnel. I hope you know what you're doing.
This will be reviewed. I want that noted.
...Fine. I'll wait. But someone is going to hear about this.
You just made a very serious mistake.
I didn't think a civilian post would actually...
Hm. Didn't see that coming from you.
I will be filing an incident report the moment I am released. That is a promise.
Noted. Protested. Being complied with under official objection.
Do you have any idea what rank you are detaining right now? Any idea at all?
…Didn’t think a post like this would actually follow through…
For the record… I still don’t think… your paperwork… was in order…
Carry on… You’re more competent… than you look…
Where are you coming from?
End of rotation. Eastern sector, twelve-hour cycle. That is all your form needs.
Perimeter sweep. We extended it east after the incident. Second crossing today. Read the memos.
Lockdown rotation. Command sends me, I go. Sector designation is not for civilian records.
Home leave. Two weeks at my mother's in Batumi. My unit is on stand-down until November.
The eastern post. Full staff, all quiet. Nothing has happened out there. Nothing at all.
The barracks. Just me. I have always been posted alone. There is no unit.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
No. Next question.
None I am required to disclose to civilian personnel. Double rotations. Men get tired. Move on.
Headaches. No sleep in three days. Everyone has that now. It is not a symptom, it is the situation.
No. Twenty years in uniform and never once on the sick list. Stamp it.
None. We are back on single eight-hour shifts. Everyone in the unit sleeps fine.
None. Command ran full medical checks this morning. Clear orders, clear chain. Everything is in order.
This checkpoint runs three seconds slower than the eastern one. I have timed it.
Civilian checkpoints waste more time than they save. Not a criticism. An observation.
Check the papers. That is all this needs to be.
The east post went quiet two days ago. Nobody told me why. I did not ask.
Command communication has been intermittent. We operate on last known orders.
You are still at your post. Good. Some of them are not.
Orders are still orders when the chain of command is unclear. Proceed.
I have been through a lot of checkpoints today. This is the last one I recognize.
Do your job, officer. That is all either of us can do now.
